dehydrated_text:
Promising all kinds of good things, but I did not want to do it. And in this way, I did similar things whenever I could. So certain things that you will notice about the story is first of all, he has contempt for Jews. A learned Jewish scholar shows that it's very easy to trick these people because their strict adherence to laws makes them stupid and ignorant. You control people by using their own laws against them.

To Jacob Frank, he said, "You can't use a knife." Then Jacob Frank responded, "Well then why is there a knife in your pocket?" While he wasn't looking, Jacob Frank put the knife into his pocket, which was just a simple magic trick. You can use these slight of hand tricks to control and manipulate people because they are stupid and ignorant.

The learned Jewish scholar said, "You must be the Messiah. You must be divine." J replied, "No, you're too stupid to follow me. Goodbye."

This story is very amusing and memorable. If I tell you this story, even when you turn 80 years old, you would still remember it. The story will shape your view of the world, showing that people are fundamentally stupid and superstitious, and you must take advantage of that.

Traveling with Zakuboski from Salonika to Poland, there prevailed a pestilence in Podolia. We came to one township where the plague was affecting the people, and we lacked food, wine, bread, cheese, etc. Remembering that those contaminated with plague do not take money, I told him the opposite: go purchase everything but don't give them money. He did just that. He went to the baker, bargained for bread, put it in his sack, but when he had to pay, the baker fell down and died. He went to the shopkeeper where he bargained for cheese, put the cheese away, and the shopkeeper died.

He then went to buy vodka from a store, where the same happened with the owner. Coming back to me where I was waiting, a rider on horseback knocked him down with his horse. "What are you doing?" shouted Jaguoski. "Are you going to ride right over me?" He didn't even finish saying it when the rider toppled over and fell to the ground. "This is how it is. I did all this because it was promised to me that no plague, nothing at all, could get at me. Therefore, all my orders were carried out successfully by the hand of the one whom I signed, and so should you be."

Your stories can be interpreted both literally and metaphorically. Literally, when people are afraid, you take advantage of their fear. When people are afraid to buy things, you go buy them. If people see the plague, it's an opportunity to make money for yourself. That's a literal interpretation. But then the spiritual perspective is remembering Jesus saying that the world is a corpse, and if you see it as such, you can stand above people. J says if you see the world as a corpse, you can do whatever you want; you can take advantage of people because they are below you.

As long as you believe that I'm above you, okay, you're a dead body. I can take everything from you, and you will always triumph. This is the idea of justification by sin: how do you know you truly believe in God? By breaking the laws of man. These conventions keep you back; what matters is your relationship with God. You have true faith, and you can do whatever you want, conquer the world, and God will let you because you have faith in God.

I asked Rabbi Isahar and Rabbi Mandach that if the second belonged to the divine why did he die.
